topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: load test: sometimes onchain balance depletes before offchain budget
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body: We budget transactions offchain so we can proactively shut down the test before spending too much eth. When the onchain and offchain budgets start with the same amount of eth, we may never hit an overdraft error (the stopping condition). It would be good to understand why this is.

topIssues.title: op-devstack: audit all retries and timeouts (and remove the bad ones)
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
Retries and timeouts are closely related. All retries and timeouts should be audited, and we should remove the ones that cause flakes.

Examples of things we should fix:

* Retrying with an arbitrary timeout. **Timeouts are side effects**: we should push them upwards in the call stack as we do with opening files, or at least make them configurable. When an operation is supposed to occur before a specific timestamp that we can compute based on protocol parameters, we should compute that timestamp and use it.
* Retrying with an arbitrary an arbitrary sleep. Same notes/caveats as in the timeout case.
* Retrying due to errors that should be handled at a lower level of abstraction (e.g., 429s should be backed-off and retried by an HTTP client, not an Ethereum JSON RPC client). Scope-creep is a risk if done as part of the op-devstack PR: we can leave it to a follow-up if necessary.
* Blindly retrying when an operation should succeed immediately.

topIssues.title: op-devstack: tracking issue for fixing acceptance test flake root-causes
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
Acceptance tests frequently flake on persistent devnets. In addition to writing new tests in a defensive style that is resilient to subtle environment changes (such as the ), we can make some changes to `op-devstack` that reduce flakes across the board. These are listed in sub-issues.

Writing acceptance tests is like writing normal go programs with syntactic sugar for common error handling and blockchain operations. It is less like writing traditional unit tests, where environmental factors like response times are irrelevant.

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): implement block builder failsafe and interop filter integration
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Implements the block builder failsafe (item 5 from #19411) and integrates op-reth with the op-interop-filter for end-to-end acceptance testing.

- **Failsafe polling:** Background task polls `admin_getFailsafeEnabled` every 1s. On transition to enabled, immediately evicts all interop txs from the pool. Matches op-geth's `startBackgroundInteropFailsafeDetection`.
- **Failsafe ingress rejection:** Cached `AtomicBool` on `SupervisorClient` provides a fast-path reject at ingress without an RPC round-trip.
- **Belt-and-suspenders eviction:** The existing block-event maintenance loop also checks failsafe state, catching any tx that raced past ingress or was added between poll ticks.
- **Validity window alignment:** `TRANSACTION_VALIDITY_WINDOW_SECS` changed from 3600 to 86400 to match op-geth's `ingressFilterTxValidityWindow`. The 600s revalidation window in the maintenance loop remains the real control.
- **Devstack integration:** In-process op-interop-filter with TCP proxy pattern to solve the EL↔filter circular startup dependency. The new `WithInteropFilter()` option on `TwoL2SupernodeInterop` presets enables devstack sysgo tests to run both op-reth and the op-interop-filter together inside acceptance tests, with direct access to toggle failsafe state without admin RPC/JWT.
- **Acceptance tests:** 4 new tests covering valid ingress, invalid ingress rejection, full failsafe lifecycle (enable → block → disable → recover), and non-interop tx unaffected during failsafe.

### Issue progress

| # | Item | Status |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | Transaction identification | Already on `develop` |
| 2 | Ingress filter | Already on `develop`; this PR aligns validity window to 86400s |
| 3 | Periodic re-validation | Already on `develop` |
| 4 | Reorg eviction (#19567) | Already on `develop` |
| 5 | Block builder failsafe | **This PR** |

## Test plan

- [ ] `TestInteropFilter_IngressAcceptsValid` — valid cross-chain tx passes through filter and reaches cross-safe
- [ ] `TestInteropFilter_IngressRejectsInvalid` — fabricated access list entry is explicitly rejected (not timeout)
- [ ] `TestInteropFilter_FailsafeLifecycle` — tx succeeds → enable failsafe → tx rejected → disable failsafe → tx recovers
- [ ] `TestInteropFilter_NonInteropUnaffected` — regular transfers succeed on both chains during failsafe
- [ ] `just lint` and `just fmt-fix` pass in `rust/`
- [ ] `go vet` and `go fmt` pass for changed Go packages

Closes #19411

topPRs.title: fix(kona): conditionally deploy `CrossL2Inbox` and dep set introduction
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Fixes **#19311**: state divergence between `kona-node` and `op-node` on single-chain Interop activation.

op-node emits 7 always-on Interop predeploy txs and 2 gated `CrossL2Inbox` txs (gated on `len(depSet.Chains()) > 1`). 

kona-node was emitting all 9 unconditionally, so single-chain deployments injected 2 extra deposit txs → divergent post-state from the first Interop block.

Go reference: `op-node/rollup/derive/interop_upgrade_transactions.go` (split) + `attributes.go:178` (the
gate).

## Operator action required

This PR adds a new CLI flag on `kona-node`:

`--interop.dependency-set` or the env: `KONA_NODE_INTEROP_DEPENDENCY_SET`

**You must supply this flag on any chain whose rollup config has `interop_time` set.**
The node will refuse to start otherwise, with a clear error:

> Interop is scheduled for this chain (interop_time = Some(...)), but
> `--interop.dependency-set` was not provided. Supply the dependency-set JSON
> file matching op-node's `--interop.dependency-set` to avoid silent state
> divergence on interop activation.

Pre-interop chains (`interop_time = None`) are unaffected. The flag is optional.

**Parity with op-node:** the flag name matches `op-node`'s `--interop.dependency-set`, and the JSON schema is the same (`kona-interop::DependencySet`). The env var name is `KONA_NODE_INTEROP_DEPENDENCY_SET` rather than `OP_NODE_…` (different binary).

## The fix

- `Interop::deposits()` now emits only the 7 always-on txs; `Interop::cross_l2_inbox_deposits()` is a separate
 path for the 2 gated txs.
- `StatefulAttributesBuilder` takes an `Option<Arc<DependencySet>>` and gates the CrossL2Inbox pair on `dependencies.len() > 1`, matching op-node's `attributes.go:178`.
- Constructor panics if `interop_time.is_some() && dependency_set.is_none()` — silent divergence becomes a
startup crash.
- Dep set plumbed through `OnlinePipeline` (live node), `OraclePipeline` (fault proof), and
`RollupNodeBuilder`.
- Fault-proof single-chain client passes `None`; interop transition passes `Some(boot.dependency_set)`.
- Stale `interop_tx_{0..3}.hex` fixtures deleted; replaced by `interop_base_tx_{0..6}.hex` +
`interop_cross_l2_inbox_tx_{0..1}.hex`.

## Tests

- `test_prepare_payload_with_interop_single_chain` — asserts 8 txs (1 L1 info + 7 base, no CrossL2Inbox).
- `test_prepare_payload_with_interop_multi_chain` — asserts 10 txs (1 L1 info + 7 base + 2 CrossL2Inbox).
- Golden fixture tests pin encoded bytes against op-node's output.

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: unskip and migrate interop acceptance tests to supernode
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Migrate the bulk of skipped interop acceptance tests from the deprecated op-supervisor presets (`NewSimpleInterop`, `NewMultiSupervisorInterop`, `NewSingleChainInterop`) to op-supernode presets (`NewTwoL2SupernodeInterop`, `TwoL2SupernodeFollowL2`, `NewSimpleInteropSupernodeProofs`), unskipping them in the process.

This brings **~30 previously-skipped tests** back online and eliminates all running test usage of old supervisor-backed presets.

Also fixes the devstack supernode preset so that `delaySeconds > 0` no longer incorrectly uses `WithForkAtGenesis(Interop)`, which was causing tests with delayed interop activation to activate interop at genesis instead.

Related to #19010.

> [!TIP]
> Each commit migrates a small group of related tests, so it may be easier to review commit-by-commit rather than the full diff.

## Changes by commit

1. **`0e12c3578d` — Bulk migration and unskip**
   - 11 message tests, 4 smoke tests, 1 contract test, 3 load tests
   - Field renames (`L2ChainA` → `L2A`, `L2CLA` → `L2ACL`, etc.) and supervisor API swaps to CL-based equivalents

2. **`bc778025fc` — Reorg tests**
   - `TestReorgUnsafeHead`, `TestReorgInitExecMsg`: migrated to supernode, unskipped

3. **`339909c784` — Upgrade tests**
   - `TestPostInbox`, `TestPostInteropUpgradeComprehensive`: migrated to `NewTwoL2SupernodeInterop`

4. **`455624edc3` — Singlechain upgrade test**
   - `TestPostInbox` (singlechain): migrated to `NewSingleChainInteropSupernodeProofs`

5. **`42e57318ee` — Sequencing window**
   - `TestSequencingWindowExpiry`: migrated to supernode, added `WithBatcherOption` support to `twoL2SupernodeInteropPresetSupportedOptionKinds`

6. **`df474b80a4` — P2P sync**
   - `TestL2CLSyncP2P`: migrated to `NewTwoL2SupernodeFollowL2` (follow-source preset with light CL followers)

7. **`95cce8299b` — CL resync**
   - `TestL2CLResync`: fixed CL stop/start sequence on supernode, unskipped

8. **`f2dbf05027` — Interop filter**
   - `TestExecMessageInvalidAttributes`: unskipped with interop filter for op-reth tx validation

9. **`bedc4fb7ba` — Supernode activation**
   - `TestSupernodeInteropActivationAfterGenesis`: unskipped (already on supernode, was marked flaky)

10. **`74958e9051`, `177bc2299d` — Pre-interop upgrade**
    - `TestPreNoInbox`: migrated to supernode with 24h activation delay to avoid flakiness at the interop boundary; added local-safe derivation check (verifies batcher→L1→supernode pipeline works pre-interop)
    - `TestUnscheduledInterop`: deleted — behavior fully covered by `TestPreNoInbox`

11. **`f5f2cdb307` — Supervisor smoke → Supernode**
    - `TestInteropSystemSupervisor` → `TestInteropSystemSupernode`: migrated and renamed, polls CL `SyncStatus().FinalizedL1` instead of supervisor RPC

12. **`d15846dfcb` — Withdrawal proofs**
    - `TestSuperRootWithdrawal`: migrated from `NewSimpleInteropSuperProofs` to `NewSimpleInteropSupernodeProofs`
    - Added `optionKindTimeTravel` to `supernodeProofsPresetSupportedOptionKinds` and wired `runtime.TimeTravel` through the supernode proofs preset constructors

## Full list of migrated/unskipped tests

| Test | Package |
|---|---|
| `TestInteropHappyTx` | `message` |

| `TestExecMsgDifferEventIndexInSingleTx` | `message` |
| `TestExecMessageInvalidAttributes` | `message` |
| `TestInteropSystemSupervisor` → `TestInteropSystemSupernode` | `message` |
| `TestInteropSystemNoop` | `smoke` |
| `TestSmokeTest` | `smoke` |
| `TestSmokeTestFailure` | `smoke` |
| `TestWrapETH` | `smoke` |
| `TestRegularMessage` | `contract` |
| `TestMaxExecutingMessagesBurst` | `loadtest` |
| `TestRelaySteady` | `loadtest` |
| `TestRelayBurst` | `loadtest` |
| `TestReorgUnsafeHead` | `reorgs` |
| `TestReorgInitExecMsg` | `reorgs` |
| `TestSequencingWindowExpiry` | `seqwindow` |

| `TestPostInbox` | `upgrade-singlechain` |
| `TestL2CLSyncP2P` | `sync` |
| `TestL2CLResync` | `sync` |
| `TestSupernodeInteropActivationAfterGenesis` | `supernode/interop/activation` |
| `TestSuperRootWithdrawal` | `proofs/withdrawal` |
| `TestUnscheduledInterop` | `prep` (deleted, subsumed by `TestPreNoInbox`) |

## Still skipped (4 tests on old presets)

| Test | Preset | Blocker |
|---|---|---|
| `TestL2ReorgAfterL1Reorg` | `NewSimpleInterop` | Supernode cross-safe stalls after deep L1 reorg — see #20134 |

It's unclear to me if we want these three remaining `NewMultiSupervisorInterop` tests migrated or deleted/rewritten.

- `TestSequencingWindowExpiry` (`interop/seqwindow`) — migrated by this PR, timing-sensitive 3–5 min test

topPRs.title: feat(kona-hardforks): add NUT bundle types and deposit tx conversion
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds NUT (Network Upgrade Transaction) bundle types and conversion logic to `kona-hardforks`, enabling future forks to define upgrade transactions as data rather than hardcoded Rust structs.

- `NutBundle` / `NetworkUpgradeTransaction` types for representing parsed bundle data
- `to_deposit_transactions()` converts bundles to `TxDeposit`s with qualified intent source hashes (`"{fork} {index}: {intent}"`)
- `to_encoded_transactions()` produces EIP-2718 encoded bytes for `Hardfork::txs()`

Stacked on #20051.
